evidence: The task and frozen template test.sh are byte-identical SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa, matching the indexed original controls. Independently hashed all 181 shared-harness artifacts, all 6 liveness-control artifacts and all 5 current source-check artifacts: no mismatches. Static comparison confirms current reward/cleanup functions and helper-generation block occur unchanged in the original control scripts; the suite tail is identical after only its scorer-path substitution. Current score.py SHA256 13de2b3885967e22aa13ded3bf33c354e3e741e85be871612c04e996eef5c04e and scoring.toml SHA256 95f70d6e06aae5e765b2309d88c444aa36d4cd82763ea2212781b6a99311bbba equal the control copies. Positive: task/tests/test.sh:60-61 writes zero before grading and installs the EXIT trap; :68-83 rejects missing entry/symlink escape; :104-111 launches UID 65534 with env -i; :115-125 probes readiness; :213-227 orders gates before scored. Indexed shell syntax has returncode 0. Existing successful synthetic suite control yields 0.7000 and failed-product gate yields 0 with scored skipped. Confirmed defect 1: task/tests/test.sh:224-225 exits immediately when the scored suite fails, bypassing score.py and write_zero_reward. The gate-only result already written at :217 remains graded=1/no_op=0. Original scored_error and scored_timeout controls retain reward=0, gates_passed=1, graded=1, no_op=0 (original-scored_error/logs/reward.json:7-12), despite evaluator failure. This conflicts with staged-task-contract.md:109 requiring plain zero on failure and misattributes evaluator failure to a graded submission. Confirmed defect 2: task/tests/test.sh:153-169 proceeds after a five-second SIGTERM wait without proving termination, overwrites app.pid, then accepts any HTTP responder (:170-183). Original term_ignored control reports exit 0/ready=1 but old_alive=true, old and after PID=34, volatile-marker retained; app-restart.log:5 records EADDRINUSE for the replacement and :21 still says ready=1. This undermines the complete-process-restart requirement in integration.md:9 and the durability evidence. Confirmed defect 3: cleanup waits without a bound at task/tests/test.sh:37 before ensure_reward at :39. The exact extracted cleanup with an ignoring child timed out after 10.012 seconds and required external kill; its initial zero reward existed, so this is a completion defect, not evidence that the reward file was absent. Additional bounded liveness concern: test.sh:50 and :138 call urlopen(..., timeout=2).read() without a wall-clock deadline. Hash-bound liveness control stdout.log:1 shows successful read after 3.5188 seconds under a two-second socket timeout. This proves the timeout is not a whole-response bound; an indefinitely trickling body can stall before the suite. This control was an expression test, not full launcher execution. These are existing extracted/synthetic controls, not configured judge results. No provider/process-security probes were run or repeated. Full configured judge and completed isolation measurements remain unavailable; no Oracle, model or portal claim is made.
counterexample: Broken app: keep saved snippets only in process memory and install a SIGTERM handler that leaves the server alive. The existing original-term_ignored control demonstrates that restart_app can report success while the same PID and volatile marker survive, allowing apparent restart-durability evidence for a non-durable app. Conforming alternative: an otherwise correct durable app can pass gates, then encounter a judge/RewardKit timeout or error; the current tail reports graded=1/no_op=0 and zero functional credit without completed scoring. An ordinary graceful-shutdown handler that takes longer than five seconds also faces an overlapping replacement and false readiness. An app that ignores SIGTERM can keep EXIT cleanup waiting indefinitely.
suggested_fix: Escalate these shared-template defects to the harness owner; preserve task/template bytes until an authorized shared fix. The shared fix should bound process shutdown and force termination when needed, verify old-process exit and replacement-process readiness before reporting restart success, bound readiness by elapsed time, and write the defined evaluator-failure zero/no-op record on any scored-suite failure while retaining diagnostics. Freeze a new candidate and rerun targeted controls after authorized changes; do not alter scoring policy or increase budgets to hide the failures.
